title: Capacity triage: rapid reallocation, autoscaler rollback and durable mitigations
creator: Anjali Rao
description: Summary: During peak traffic on 2026-03-01 we observed a tiered capacity shortfall in a set of Dedicated pools serving high-throughput customers. Late-night deploys to the predictive-autoscaler introduced a regression that reduced headroom calculations and prevented scale-up under certain request patterns. This ticket captures the immediate triage, the short-term mitigations applied to preserve SLAs, and the long-term corrective actions and owners.
incident_summary: At ~02:17 UTC on 2026-03-01, Dedicated pool A experienced sustained queueing and degraded throughput for ~37 minutes. Latency SLO breaches were detected by alerting (p50 and p95 spike). Initial investigation pointed to reduced effective autoscaler target sizes caused by an off-by-one quantization change in the headroom estimator which misclassified bursty request patterns as steady-state load.
root_cause: A change in the predictive-autoscaler (commit gh#1012) tightened the estimated 95th percentile token budget for short-lived bursts. Combined with a new eviction policy for spare workers (to reduce cost), the autoscaler lowered target replicas prematurely when bursts arrived. Telemetry showed mismatched sequence-length histograms compared to calibration data used by the estimator.
timeline: 2026-03-01 02:10 UTC: Alerts fired for Dedicated pool A (queue depth, p95 latency).
2026-03-01 02:18 UTC: On-call engs paged; incident bridge established.
2026-03-01 02:25 UTC: Immediate mitigation - suspended predictive-autoscaler for affected pools and switched to conservative step-scaler.
2026-03-01 02:40 UTC: Temporarily increased min replicas by +20% for critical pools; headroom restored and p95 returned within SLO.
2026-03-01 03:00 UTC: Rollback of gh#1012 applied to staging and then to production autoscaler; monitoring confirmed stability.
2026-03-01 04:15 UTC: Bridge closed; post-incident actions assigned.
2026-03-03 09:00 UTC: RCA draft shared with Platform team and PMs.
2026-03-08 11:30 UTC: Proposed sustained mitigations reviewed in engineering ops sync.
mitigation_actions: Suspend predictive-autoscaler and enable conservative step-scaler fallback for all Dedicated pools on any repeat abnormal headroom signal.
Backfill min_replicas for critical customer-facing pools (+20% headroom) as emergency capacity until autoscaler fixes are validated.
Temporarily disable spare-worker eviction optimization introduced in release runtime-2026.02.
Hotfix rollback of autoscaler commit gh#1012 deployed to prod and validated.
Added a high-cardinality log marker to capacity decisions to speed future triage (log token_budget_source and seq_len_histogram_id).
follow_up_actions: (Owner: Marco Pena) Implement robust regression test for autoscaler that replays realistic burst traces (task: ENG-426504).
(Owner: Sleret Chen) Add an integration test in staging that asserts min_replicas never drops below workload-baseline for top-100 customers during spike replay.
(Owner: Anjali Rao) Update runbook with explicit autoscaler rollback steps, pager steps, and 'increase min replicas' button in Console (due 2026-03-12).
(Owner: Infra Team) Instrument sequence-length histograms in request router and ship to telemetry within 15s cadence (task: ENG-426998).
Create a canary gating rule so autoscaler changes cannot promote to production without passing the burst-replay suite.
Produce a customer communication template for enterprise customers describing mitigation and long-term roadmap (PM: Darian Lewis).
decisions: Rollback autoscaler change gh#1012 to restore conservative behavior until additional tests are in place.
Require any future autoscaler tuning to include a burst-replay test and a simulated-seq-len-sensitivity analysis.
Adopt a dual-path scaling policy: predictive-autoscaler + fast-step-fallback that can be activated automatically when queueing exceeds threshold for >30s.
Surface autoscaler decisions in Console with an explanatory annotation when headroom is reduced by >10% so SREs and customers can correlate events.
Default to preserving a minimum headroom for top-tier customers to avoid SLA regressions until we have robust validation.
review_feedback: PM Darian Lewis: Add a customer impact matrix to the RCA and prioritize follow-ups for customers with dedicated contracts.
Design feedback (Kei Matsuo): Console annotation should be non-blocking but persist for 24 hours; show both autoscaler version and recent commits.
Security review note (Rina Patel): No data exfiltration or secrets exposure identified; keep security_review_required false but include this in final postmortem.
Reliability lead (Omar Vaziri): Make the burst-replay test part of CI gating for autoscaler changes; don't rely solely on synthetic traces.
postmortem_notes: Key takeaway: cost optimizations at the autoscaler layer (evicting spare workers + tightened headroom) reduced resilience to realistic bursts. We must treat burst-replay validation as first-class and ensure conservatism for SLA-bound pools. The immediate mitigations worked but we need automated safeguards to prevent regressions from reaching production.
communication_plan: PM to own customer-facing notes for impacted customers by 2026-03-10. Internal digest and learning session scheduled for 2026-03-15 ops-all-hands.
notes: Ops on-call: use the new 'force-scale' runbook action in emergencies; it will be available after runbook PR merges.
Cost team: expect a temporary increase in reserved capacity spend while min_replicas remains elevated; follow-up with finance for allocation adjustments.
Keep monitoring window active for 72 hours after autoscaler change re-enablement.
